body:
@ngocdaothanh 
I tested it with master, but probably it similar in other branches.
The problem is either
- https://github.com/netty/netty/blob/master/example/src/main/java/io/netty/example/http/websocketx/server/WebSocketServerHandler.java#L97 has to be set to true to support extensions

or
- https://github.com/netty/netty/blob/master/example/src/main/java/io/netty/example/http/websocketx/server/WebSocketServerInitializer.java#L44 should be removed

I don't know if the example should be simply fixed or if the library should be patched to avoid the problem. However I don't see a good way for that because how the Extension Negotiation is implemented. The `WebSocketServerExtensionHandler` does not know the actual handshaker and can thereby not ask whether extensions are allowed whether it should take actions or not. Maybe the handshaker could scan the pipeline when extensions are not allowed and when it finds an `WebSocketServerExtensionHandler` it could provide an error message that the pipeline is configure in an invalid way.

repository.name: netty
repository.description: Netty project - an event-driven asynchronous network application framework

issue.body:
Motivation:
As report in #2953 the websocket server example contained a bug and did therefore not work with chrome:
A websocket extension is added to the pipeline but extensions were disallowed in the handshaker and decoder,
which is leading the decoder to closing the connection after receiving an extension frame.

Modifications:
Allow websocket extensions in the handshaker to correctly enable the extension.

Result:
Working websocket server example
Fixes #2953

issue.body:
Google Chrome 57.0.2987.133 fails to connect to the Netty WebSocket, giving this error:

WebSocket connection to 'ws://localhost:4081/' failed: Error during WebSocket handshake: Sent non-empty 'Sec-WebSocket-Protocol' header but no response was received

Safari Technolgy Preview 27 and Firefox 53.0b8 are able to connect without error. Chrome doesn't have a problem with connecting through [websockify](https://github.com/novnc/websockify) to the Python server, so this points to some kind of interoperability incompatibility issue perhaps with Netty 4.1.9.Final or how I am using it.
